sources.entry: RSS2EMail - Fetches RSS/Atom-feeds and pushes new content to any email-receiver, supports OPML. GPL-2.0 Python/deb

summary.one_liner: rss2email is a Python command-line tool that fetches RSS/Atom feeds and emails new entries to you, with OPML support.
summary.what_it_does: The r2e command subscribes to feeds, checks them on each run, and emails any entries it has not seen before, tracking seen items in a JSON feed database. Feeds are added with "r2e add", and the README mentions OPML support as a feature. Delivery can go through a local sendmail program or directly via SMTP or LMTP, with TLS/SSL and STARTTLS options. Entries can be converted to plain text or sent as HTML mail. A post-processing hook lets you modify each entry before it is sent, and built-in processors are named for prettifying HTML and removing redirects on post URLs. The README describes running it on a schedule via cron on Unix/Linux or Windows Task Scheduler.
use_cases: get blog or news updates delivered to email
subscribe to feeds without a feed reader app
email new RSS entries on a schedule with cron
import a feed list from OPML
send feed items as HTML or plain-text mail
strip tracking redirects from feed links
how_to_run: Ensure Python 3.6 or newer is installed, plus feedparser and html2text (or use a distribution package).
Download the source and run: pip install . from the unpacked directory.
Create a config and feed database: r2e new you@yourdomain.com
Edit the generated config file to set SMTP options if no local sendmail is available.
Subscribe to a feed: r2e add <feed-url-or-name>
Run r2e run --no-send first to mark existing items as seen, then schedule r2e run (e.g. via cron).
notable: Emails new feed entries directly to your inbox, no web interface required
Post-processor hook for modifying entries before sending
Can send through local sendmail, SMTP (with STARTTLS/SMTPS), or LMTP
Packaged for many Linux distributions, BSDs, and NixOS
caveats: Requires a working sendmail or an SMTP/LMTP server to deliver mail
Scheduling must be set up separately (cron or Windows Task Scheduler)
The README does not describe a web interface or a hosted service
keywords: send feed items as html mail
